title: Opportunistic request triage and staged readiness windows to stabilize multi-region SLOs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During cross-region failovers and sudden regional load spikes we observe cascading autoscaler churn and readiness flapping that causes elevated tail latency and SLO breaches for a subset of high-priority routes. Existing readiness gating is binary and global; it does not allow per-priority admission or progressive backpressure.

Goal: Implement a system to triage incoming requests opportunistically and open staged readiness windows (priority lanes) so that: 1) critical/paid traffic maintains SLOs during degradation, 2) autoscaler stability is improved by smoothing readiness signals and reducing thrash, and 3) circuit breakers at regional boundaries can gracefully shed lower-priority work without causing global failover.

Proposal summary: 1) Introduce priority-based readiness lanes on the agent side that map token/request classes to graded readiness gates (green/yellow/red) with configurable budgets. 2) Implement short, sliding readiness windows (e.g., 30s/2m/5m) where readiness transitions are rate-limited and require quorum of health signals across local and peer-region probes before allowing scale-down. 3) Add opportunistic request triage at the frontend router: requests evaluated by token priority and SLA tier are admitted into lanes; lower-priority lanes are queued or rerouted to fallbacks when a lane is in yellow/red. 4) Extend regional circuit orchestration to broadcast lane state and a compact degradation token to peer regions so downstream routing can make informed failover decisions without centralized coordination.

Key trade-offs and rationale:  - Complexity vs benefit: introduces a small state machine per lane and cross-region propagation; trade-off is justified because it preserves revenue-bearing traffic and reduces autoscaler oscillation costs.  - Consistency vs speed: lane state propagation is eventual (sub-5s) using compact deltas to avoid coupling; this allows fast local decisions while peer regions inform routing heuristics.  - Cost: may slightly increase p99 latency for low-priority traffic but reduces overall 99.9/99.99 SLO risk for high-priority routes.

Deliverables: design doc, agent runtime changes for lane gating, router triage logic, regional circuit broadcast protocol (compact JSON delta), autoscaler adapter to respect lane-inferred demand smoothing, console dashboards for per-lane health & cost impact, e2e chaos tests and canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: High-priority traffic (as defined by routing tags) maintains pre-degradation p99 within 10% during injected regional load tests
Autoscaler scale-down/scale-up event frequency reduces by >=30% under sustained noisy probes compared to baseline
Readiness transitions are rate-limited and observable; no more than 3 flips within any 5m window for healthy instances
Regional circuit broadcasts successfully reach peer regions within 5s in 95% of cases in staging tests
Rollout can be toggled per-region and per-customer via feature flag without restarts
implementation_notes: Agent change: add lane table keyed by (route, priority) with state machine and cooldown timers
Router change: add token-priority evaluator and admission queue; expose fast path header so backend can short-circuit low-latency lanes
Autoscaler adapter: introduce smoothed demand estimator that consumes lane-state to avoid immediate scale-down when many lanes briefly flip
Circuit broadcast: use existing gossip channel with new compact 'laneDelta' envelope to avoid new long-lived RPCs
DB/config: new per-customer lane policies stored in config service; add migration and defaults for existing customers
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): unit tests and runtime integration on local harness; validate lane state machine determinism
Stage 2 (staging): enable for non-critical routes in us-west-2; run synthetic regional failover tests and canary traffic
Stage 3 (limited prod): opt-in for a small set of enterprise customers in single-region -> multi-region failover windows
Stage 4 (ramp): increase coverage, monitor SLO and autoscaler churn metrics, rollback criteria defined
Final: GA behind console toggle with per-customer defaults and docs
testing: Unit tests for lane state machine transitions and cooldown logic
Integration: hairpin on local cluster simulating 3-region mesh and verifying lane deltas
Chaos: drop 40% of probe signals in one region and assert high-priority p99 stays within threshold
Load: sustained 2x baseline QPS and verify autoscaler smoothing prevents >2x oscillation
Canary: gradual PID-controlled rollout with automatic rollback on SLO breach
